worst_prec = _transferred.loc[_transferred["precision_pct"].idxmax()]

worst_var, next_var = _by_var.iloc[0], _by_var.iloc[1]

# Purpose and scope

`{python} COMPANY` is transferring the `{python} PRODUCT` drug substance process from
`{python} SENDING_SITE` to `{python} RECEIVING_SITE`, and this plan defines the scope of
that transfer, the activities it comprises, and the deliverables that must be complete
before process performance qualification can start at the receiving site. The process
moves as a whole. No unit operation is redeveloped at the receiving site, and no set-point
changes by the act of being transferred.

Technology transfer is an element of the pharmaceutical quality system, and it is
expected to deliver the knowledge that allows the receiving site to run the process as it
was intended to run [@ichq10]. It is also the point at which the Stage 1 process design
work is consolidated for a commercial process [@fda2011]. The receiving site has to
operate inside ranges that data support, so the transfer and the process characterization
campaign are planned as one programme. This plan is the parent of that campaign and
states why each of its documents exists.

The package contains `{python} n_docs` controlled documents, and @tbl-package lists all of
them except this plan. A pre-characterization risk assessment (RA-001) fixes the scope of
the studies, a master plan (PCMP-001) sets the approach that every study shares, a plan
and a report cover each unit operation (PCP-003 through PCP-010, PCR-003 through PCR-010),
and a master report (PCMR-001) consolidates the outcome for the process as a whole. Each
of those documents is a deliverable of this transfer, and the sequence in which they are
produced is given in §10.

```{python}
#| output: asis
print(corpus_docs_md(DOC))
print()
print(": The A-Mab document package that this transfer plan parents. {#tbl-package}")
```

The scope of this plan is the drug substance process, Steps `{python} step_first` to
`{python} step_last`, as it will be operated at the receiving site. Three things sit
outside it. Drug product manufacture and fill-finish are not covered, and neither is cell
bank manufacture and testing. The execution of process performance qualification is not
covered either, although §7 states what that stage requires and when it may begin, because
the readiness decision belongs to this plan even though the qualification itself does not.

# Product and process description

`{python} PRODUCT` is a humanized IgG1 monoclonal antibody produced in mammalian cell
culture, and its main mechanism of action is antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity, so
the glycan attributes that modulate effector function carry an efficacy risk and are
treated as quality attributes throughout the process [@amab2009]. The purification train is the
platform train that has already supported three products of the same class (X-Mab, Y-Mab
and Z-Mab). What moves to the receiving site is therefore a platform process, and the
platform history is part of the knowledge that moves with it.

The drug substance process comprises `{python} n_steps` unit operations, numbered Steps
`{python} step_first` to `{python} step_last`, and it begins with a fed-batch culture at a
working volume of `{python} scale_l` L. Purification follows the platform sequence of
Protein A capture, low pH viral inactivation, cation exchange, anion exchange, small
virus retentive filtration and ultrafiltration with diafiltration into the formulation
buffer. The final step delivers drug substance at a target concentration of
`{python} ds_conc` g/L, and @tbl-train lists every step with the role it holds in the
control strategy.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(train)
print()
print(": The A-Mab drug substance process train and the role of each step. {#tbl-train}")
```

The bioreactor forms most of the attributes the process has to control, since
`{python} n_cqa_bio` of the `{python} n_cqa` attributes in the register are set there, and
they include the glycans, the charge variants, aggregate and the impurity burden that the
purification train then clears. The downstream steps remove impurities and virus without
changing the glycan distribution, and Protein A capture in particular sets one attribute of
its own, leached Protein A, and is the principal clearance step for host cell protein (HCP)
and DNA. Cation exchange is the principal aggregate polish. Anion exchange is a
flow-through polish that clears XMuLV, host cell protein and DNA.

Viral safety is modular. Clearance comes from `{python} n_viral_steps` steps whose
mechanisms are independent of one another, namely inactivation at low pH (Step 6),
adsorption of virus at anion exchange (Step 8), and size-based retention at the virus
filter (Step 9).
Each contribution is measured in its own study and the cumulative claim is consolidated in
PCMR-001 [@ichq5a]. No single step carries the whole claim.

Two steps neither form nor clear a quality attribute. Harvest and clarification (Step 4)
recovers the culture, and the final ultrafiltration and diafiltration step (Step 10)
concentrates the product and exchanges it into the formulation buffer. Both transfer and
qualify like every other step, but their parameters are keyed to process performance and
mass balance instead of to a quality attribute.

# Sending and receiving sites

The sending site is `{python} SENDING_SITE` and the receiving site is
`{python} RECEIVING_SITE`, and both operate under one pharmaceutical quality system, one
change control system and one deviation management system [@ichq10]. @tbl-sites gives the
activities each site holds once the transfer is complete.

| Activity | Held by |
|---|---|
| Process development and optimization | Sending site |
| Scale-down model operation and qualification | Sending site |
| Characterization studies and their reports | Sending site |
| Analytical method validation and reference materials | Sending site |
| Control strategy definition | Sending site, approved by Quality Assurance at both sites |
| Commercial manufacture of drug substance | Receiving site |
| Batch record execution and in-process control | Receiving site |
| Release and in-process testing, after method transfer | Receiving site quality control |
| Process performance qualification | Receiving site |
| Change control after handover | Receiving site, with sending site review |

: Activities held by each site after transfer. {#tbl-sites}

Development work does not stop at handover. The sending site keeps the scale-down models,
the characterization data and the analytical reference materials, so that a question
raised during qualification at the receiving site can be answered on the same model that
generated the original data. The receiving site owns execution from the point at which
the master batch record is approved, and it owns any subsequent change to the process,
with the sending site as a named reviewer.

# Site equivalency analysis

The receiving site is able to operate the process as it was developed, and that conclusion
rests on a comparison across five dimensions, namely the equipment train, the scale,
process control capability, utilities and materials, and analytical capability, with the
quality system common to both sites. @tbl-equiv gives the comparison, and two of the five
dimensions differ in a way that affects the process, each of those differences carrying an
action.

| Dimension | Sending site | Receiving site | Assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Equipment train | Scale-down model of every unit operation | Commercial train of the same class and sequence | Equivalent in class and sequence |
| Scale | Bench and pilot scale-down systems | Commercial scale (§2) | Differs by design; scale-dependent parameters matched on performance |
| Process control | Development control systems and single-unit skids | Plant control system with recipe management | Assessed per parameter against the range the process needs |
| Utilities and materials | Compendial and vendor-qualified supply | Same specifications, commercial supply chain | Equivalent, subject to vendor qualification |
| Analytical capability | Methods validated at the sending site (@tbl-sop) | Quality control laboratory, methods to be transferred | Equivalent after method transfer (§6.2) |
| Quality system | One quality system and one change control system | One quality system and one change control system | Common to both sites |

: Site equivalency comparison across the dimensions that affect the process. {#tbl-equiv}

Scale is the first difference and it is structural. The sending site holds scale-down
models of every unit operation, and the receiving site holds the commercial train, whose
production bioreactor works at `{python} scale_l` L. Parameters that are independent of
scale carry across unchanged, because they are properties of the chemistry and not of the
vessel. Culture pH, temperature, protein load, conductivity, elution pH and hold time mean
the same thing in a bench model as they do in a commercial vessel. Parameters that depend
on the geometry of the vessel or the column do not carry across in the same way, so they
are matched on the performance they produce instead of on the value set at the panel. Each
scale-down model qualification records that matching (SOP-1001), and the per-step
characterization plans (PCP-003 through PCP-010) describe it for the step they cover.

Control capability is the second difference, and it is the one that decides how tightly a
parameter has to be held. A range that is wide relative to what the equipment can hold is
a different proposition from a range the equipment can only just achieve, and the
classification scheme used across the campaign takes that into account (SOP-4001). Each
classification is therefore made against the control capability of the receiving site's
equipment, and not against what a development rig can hold. Capability is measured, not
assumed. The receiving site supplies control capability data for every parameter in
@tbl-scope, and those data are an input to the classification recorded in each
characterization report.

Utilities and raw materials were compared on grade and on supply, not on supplier
identity. The utilities the process depends on (water, process gases, clean steam) and the
consumables it depends on (buffers, media, single-use components, chromatography resins)
meet the same specifications at both sites. Materials are bought from the same vendors
wherever the vendor is qualified for commercial supply. Where a vendor is not qualified,
the substitution is handled as a raw material change under change control, together with
an assessment of the attribute that the material touches.

Analytical capability is equivalent in scope and is not yet in place. The methods the
process needs are validated at the sending site, and @tbl-sop is the register of those
validations. Each of them has to be transferred to the receiving site's quality control
laboratory and requalified there before it can support a release decision or an in-process
decision. The way that is done is set out in §6.2, and the residual risk is carried in the
gap register (@tbl-gaps).

The comparison shows that the receiving site holds equipment of the same class in the same
sequence, under the same quality system, and it fixes the control capability data the
receiving site has to supply for every parameter in @tbl-scope. It does not show that the
equipment holds every parameter to the range the process needs, which is established
parameter by parameter when those data are assessed in the characterization reports. It
does not show that the process performs identically at the two sites either, and no
comparison made on paper can show that. Equivalence of performance comes from the
comparability data described in §5 and from the qualification batches described in §7. The
design space itself is defined on qualified scale-down models and is not confirmed at
commercial scale at the edges of its ranges.

# Scale-down model and comparability strategy

The characterization that justifies the receiving site's operating ranges is executed on
qualified scale-down models and not at commercial scale. That is the usual approach for a
process of this kind, and it carries one condition. A scale-down model may support a range
claim only where it has been qualified against data at scale for the step it represents
(SOP-1001).

Qualification follows the same pattern at every step, in that variables which are
independent of scale are operated at the commercial target values, and variables which
depend on scale are set so that the small system reproduces the performance of the large
one. The model is then run at the centre point in replicate, and its input and output
attributes (titre, impurity levels, step yield, the quality attributes the step governs)
are compared with data from the development and clinical campaigns at scale. Those
replicate centre points also give the pure error term that the lack-of-fit test in each
design of experiments study needs, so model qualification and study design draw on the
same runs.

@tbl-scope gives the characterization scope for each step and names the documents that
carry it. Of the `{python} n_params` parameters in the process, `{python} n_mv` are studied
in multivariate designs and `{python} n_uv` are assessed one factor at a time. The split is
set by the pre-characterization risk assessment (RA-001) from the potential impact of a
parameter on a quality attribute and its potential to interact with other parameters, and
it is not revisited in this plan [@ichq9]. Two steps carry no multivariate study at all,
harvest and clarification (Step 4) and ultrafiltration and diafiltration (Step 10), because
neither of them forms or clears a quality attribute.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(scope)
print()
print(": Characterization scope by step, with the plan and report that cover it. {#tbl-scope}")
```

The plans that execute this scope on the scale-down models are PCP-003 through PCP-010,
one for each step, and each names the model it uses and the qualification that supports it.
@tbl-equip lists the instrumented systems the studies run on, and those systems are held
under calibration and change control at the sending site, with their calibration and
maintenance records forming part of the data package the receiving site receives.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(equipment_df()[["Equipment", "Description"]])
print()
print(": Instrumented scale-down systems used in the characterization studies. {#tbl-equip}")
```

Comparability between the sites is demonstrated on material and not on documents.
Engineering runs at the receiving site are executed at the set-points, with every parameter
inside its normal operating range, and the resulting in-process attributes, step yields and
drug substance quality attributes are compared with the sending site's data and with the
acceptance criteria in @tbl-cqa. The comparison is made step by step and then across the
train, because an impurity that three steps clear in series cannot be assessed at any one
of them alone. Where an attribute falls outside the expected distribution, the difference
is investigated and closed in the receiving site's quality system before the qualification
batches start.

# Transfer of the process, methods and control strategy

Transfer runs in three streams, which are the manufacturing process, the analytical
methods and the control strategy. Each stream has its own deliverables and its own
approval, and none of them is complete until Quality Assurance at both sites has signed
it. The streams are not independent and their sequence matters, because a method has to be
in place at the receiving site before the engineering runs can be assessed, and the control
strategy cannot be finalized until the characterization reports it draws on are approved.

## Manufacturing process

The manufacturing process transfers as a document set and as a training obligation. The
sending site issues the process description, the parameter set-points with their normal
operating ranges, the in-process control points with their action limits, and the sampling
plan for each of the `{python} n_steps` unit operations. The receiving site converts these
into its own master batch records and into the recipe configuration held in the plant
control system. Both sites then reconcile the batch record against the process description
line by line, and Manufacturing Science at each site signs the reconciliation before any
material is charged. Operator training is documented before execution.

The parameter set is what that reconciliation is checked against, and all
`{python} n_params` parameters appear in the batch record with their set-point and their
normal operating range, whatever their classification, so that an excursion is recognized
when it happens and not at batch review. Classification decides what an excursion means
and what has to be done about it, and not whether the value is recorded at all.

@tbl-sop lists the procedures and method validation records cited across the package, all
of which are sending site documents. Each of them needs an equivalent in the receiving
site's system, and the mapping between the two sets is a deliverable of the transfer (§10).

```{python}
#| output: asis
print(all_sop_table())
print()
print(": Controlled documents cited across the A-Mab characterization package. {#tbl-sop}")
```

## Analytical methods

Analytical method transfer sits on the critical path, because no batch is released and no
comparability claim is made until the receiving site's laboratory can run the methods that
measure the attributes in question. @tbl-methods gives the validated performance of the
methods for which performance records are held, which is the intermediate precision, the
limit of quantitation, the accuracy and the share of the observed variability that the
method itself contributes. The register of the validations themselves is @tbl-sop.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(methods)
print()
print(": Validated performance records held for the analytical methods. {#tbl-methods}")
```

Acceptance criteria for each method transfer are set from those records, and the receiving
site runs the method on split samples alongside the sending site, with the criterion for
agreement derived from the intermediate precision recorded in the method's validation
report. Two methods need more attention than the rest. `{python} worst_var["id"]` and
`{python} next_var["id"]` contribute the largest shares of the observed variability, at
`{python} f"{worst_var['variance_fraction']:.2f}"` and
`{python} f"{next_var['variance_fraction']:.2f}"`, and `{python} worst_prec["id"]` is also
the least precise of the methods that transfer, at
`{python} f"{worst_prec['precision_pct']:.1f}"` %RSD. Both measure impurities that the
purification train exists to clear, so a difference between the two laboratories in either
method would present as a difference in process performance.

Critical reagents are the practical risk in transferring an immunoassay. The HCP assay and
the leached Protein A assay both depend on reagent lots that are not interchangeable
without a bridging study. Reserve lots of both are held at the sending site until the
receiving site has bridged its own, and that bridging is part of the method transfer
protocol (GAP-02 in §8).

Not every method transfers. The infectivity assays for the two model viruses (XMuLV and
MVM) support the clearance studies, and viral clearance is not measured on commercial
batches at all. Clearance is claimed from spiking studies executed on qualified small-scale
models, and the commercial process is never spiked [@ichq5a]. The
receiving site therefore transfers the release and in-process methods, and takes the viral
clearance claim from the characterization package.

## Control strategy

The control strategy is what the other two streams exist to deliver, and it has four
elements, which are the parameter set-points and their ranges, the in-process controls
with their action limits, release testing against the drug substance specification, and
life-cycle controls such as resin and membrane reuse limits [@ichq11]. The receiving site
implements all four, and Quality Assurance at both sites approves the whole before the
qualification batches begin.

@tbl-cqa lists the attributes the control strategy exists to control, with the acceptance
criterion and the criticality of each. The register holds `{python} n_cqa` attributes, of
which `{python} n_cqa_crit` are of high or very high criticality, and the
`{python} n_vh` of very high criticality are high mannose and the two viral clearance
claims. Criticality is treated as a continuum and not as a binary label [@ichq9], so the
attributes at the lower end of the register stay in the control strategy and are reported,
with the depth of control proportionate to criticality.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(cqas_all)
print()
print(": Drug substance quality attributes, acceptance criteria and criticality. {#tbl-cqa}")
```

Control is distributed across the train. The glycans are formed in the bioreactor and are
not modified downstream, so their control is a culture control and is reported in PCR-003.
Aggregate is formed upstream and polished at
cation exchange (PCR-007), and host cell protein is cleared by three chromatography steps
in series, so the acceptable output of any one of them depends on what the others achieve
(PCR-005, PCR-007 and PCR-008). Viral clearance is credited from the three steps named in
§2 and is consolidated in PCMR-001. No step is credited twice.

Until PCMR-001 is approved, the classifications carried in the batch record are
provisional. The receiving site operates to the platform set-points and normal operating
ranges in the interim, which is the conservative position, and revises the batch record
when the campaign reports. This plan defines no design space and classifies no parameter,
since both are outputs of the characterization package and neither is created by the act
of transfer.

# Process performance qualification strategy

Process performance qualification is Stage 2 of the lifecycle and it follows this transfer
[@fda2011]. The receiving site manufactures `{python} n_ppq` consecutive drug substance
batches at commercial scale, at the set-points, with every parameter held inside its
normal operating range. These batches are not experiments and no parameter is varied
deliberately in them, and their purpose is to confirm that the process, as transferred and
as controlled, delivers drug substance of the required quality reproducibly in the facility
that will make it.

Qualification may start when the following are in place.

- The characterization reports for every unit operation are approved against the approach set in PCMP-001, and PCMR-001 states that the process is ready for Stage 2.
- Every method needed for in-process control and for release has been transferred to the receiving site and requalified there.
- Equipment, utility and facility qualification are complete, and the approved recipe is loaded in the plant control system.
- The engineering runs have been executed and the comparability assessment has been reviewed, with any deviation closed.
- The control strategy is approved at both sites and is reflected in the master batch record.
- The gaps named in §8 as prerequisites for qualification are closed, and each of the remaining gaps has an agreed closure plan.

Acceptance criteria for qualification are not set here, but in the qualification protocol,
where they are derived from the design space and the process capability reported in
PCMR-001 and are approved before the first batch is charged. Sampling during qualification
is more extensive than routine sampling, and the additional sampling points are specified
in the same protocol.

Stage 3 continued process verification follows qualification and sits outside this plan.
The monitoring plan that supports it uses the same parameter set and the same methods, so
it is written once PCMR-001 and the qualification report are available. Confirmation of
the design space at commercial scale accumulates over the operating life of the process,
because the qualification batches are executed at the set-points and say nothing about the
edges of the ranges.

# Gap analysis

Six gaps were identified during transfer planning, and none of them is closed at the date
of this plan. @tbl-gaps is the register, and each entry states the gap, its impact on the
process or on the data, the action that closes it, and its status. Each of the six is
discussed below, and four of them carry a residual risk that has to be explained.

| Gap | Area | Description | Impact | Mitigation | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GAP-01 | Materials | Alternate Protein A resin has no platform bridging data | Second resin cannot enter commercial use on platform data | Independent characterization per RA-004 before use | Open |
| GAP-02 | Analytical method | Critical reagent lots for the HCP and leached Protein A assays not bridged | A reagent lot difference can present as an impurity difference | Reagent bridging study during method transfer | In progress |
| GAP-03 | Validation | Design space not confirmed at commercial scale at the edges of its ranges | Operation near a range edge rests on model prediction | Qualification inside the NOR; edge moves under change control | Open |
| GAP-04 | Equipment | Scale-dependent parameters cannot be matched setting for setting | Small-scale performance may not reproduce at scale | Performance matching per SOP-1001, tested in engineering runs | In progress |
| GAP-05 | Documentation | Procedures and method validations cited are sending site documents | A batch record could cite a document the receiving site lacks | Document mapping table issued with the process description | Open |
| GAP-06 | Control strategy | Parameter classification is an output of the campaign, not yet complete | The batch record cannot yet state which parameters are critical | Interim operation to platform set-points and NORs | Open |

: Transfer gap register, with the impact and the closing action for each gap. {#tbl-gaps}

GAP-02, GAP-04 and GAP-06 close before qualification and are prerequisites for it. GAP-01
and GAP-05 constrain supply and documentation and do not block qualification, and GAP-03 is
carried into Stage 3 and is not closed by qualification at all. Two of the six are recorded
as in progress in @tbl-gaps because their mitigations have already started, with reserve
reagent lots held at the sending site (GAP-02) and the performance matching recorded as each
scale-down model is qualified (GAP-04). Closure of GAP-01 and GAP-03 is owned by Process
Development at the sending site, and closure of GAP-02 by Analytical Development at both
sites. GAP-04 is owned by Manufacturing Science at both sites, and GAP-05 and GAP-06 by
MSAT at the sending site. Quality Assurance decides in each case whether a gap is closed
(§9).

The alternate Protein A resin cannot be qualified on platform data (GAP-01), because
RA-004 assessed that resin and concluded that independent characterization is required,
with no bridging from the platform data set. The receiving site therefore begins commercial
manufacture with the primary resin alone, and the second resin enters the process only when
its own characterization is complete and approved. What remains is a constraint on supply
flexibility and not a risk to product quality, because the resin the characterization
package covers is the resin the process will use.

The design space is defined on qualified scale-down models and is not confirmed at
commercial scale at the edges of its ranges (GAP-03). Movement towards the edge of a range
at the receiving site is supported by the fitted models and by the scale-down data, and not by
experience at scale. Qualification does not close this gap, because the qualification
batches are run at the set-points with every parameter inside its normal operating range.
The gap closes as data at scale accumulate under continued process verification. A planned
move towards the edge of a range before that point is assessed prospectively under change
control, which is what movement inside a design space requires of the quality system in
any case [@ichq8; @ichq10].

The two immunoassays are the transfer risk that surfaces last (GAP-02). HCP and leached
Protein A are both measured by immunoassay, both depend on critical reagent lots, and both
report on impurities the drug substance specification covers.
`{python} worst_prec["id"]` is the least precise of the methods that transfer, so a reagent
difference between the two laboratories can look exactly like a process difference at the
step that clears the impurity. The mitigation is a reagent bridging study during method
transfer, with reserve lots held at the sending site until it is complete. Until that study
is closed, an HCP result from the receiving site is compared with the sending site's data
only alongside a split sample analysed at both.

Scale-dependent parameters are matched on the performance they produce and not setting for
setting (GAP-04), which is a weaker warrant than a direct match. The geometry of a bench
vessel and the geometry of a commercial vessel differ by construction, and a parameter that
depends on that geometry cannot be held at the same value in both. The matching is recorded
in each scale-down model qualification (SOP-1001) and is tested in the engineering runs, and
that is why those runs are a prerequisite for qualification. Where an engineering run does not reproduce the scale-down performance for a
step, the model for that step is requalified before its characterization data are used to
support a range at commercial scale.

The last two gaps are documentary. The characterization package cites sending site
procedures and method validation records while the receiving site holds its own set, so a
mapping table is issued with the process description (GAP-05). Parameter classification is
an output of the campaign, so the batch record cannot yet state which parameters are
critical (GAP-06). Both gaps close on approval of the documents they depend on. Neither
blocks the engineering runs.

# Roles and responsibilities

Three functions own the transfer between them. Process Development and Manufacturing
Science at the sending site own the process description, the characterization package and
the control strategy. Manufacturing and Manufacturing Science at the receiving site own the
batch records, the plant configuration, the engineering runs and execution. Quality
Assurance at both sites owns approval, change control and the release decision, and it is
the function that decides whether a gap is closed, with @tbl-roles giving the split by
deliverable.

| Deliverable | Sending site | Receiving site | Quality Assurance |
|---|---|---|---|
| Process description and parameter ranges | Author | Review | Approve |
| Characterization plans and reports | Author | Review | Approve |
| Scale-down model qualification records | Author | Review | Approve |
| Master batch records and recipe configuration | Review | Author | Approve |
| Analytical method transfer protocols and reports | Author | Co-author | Approve |
| Engineering runs and comparability assessment | Review | Author | Approve |
| Control strategy | Author | Review | Approve |
| Qualification protocol and report | Review | Author | Approve |
| Gap register and gap closure | Co-owner | Co-owner | Approve |

: Responsibility for each transfer deliverable. {#tbl-roles}

Where a deliverable has an author at one site and a reviewer at the other, both signatures
are required. Neither site closes a transfer deliverable on its own.

# Deliverables and schedule

The transfer is executed in five phases, each of which ends in a document that Quality
Assurance approves, and @tbl-deliv lists the deliverables in sequence. Calendar dates are
held in the project schedule and are not reproduced here, because it is the sequence and
not the date that governs. A phase is not complete until its deliverables are approved, and
phases overlap where the dependency allows.

| Phase | Deliverables | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| Planning | This transfer plan (PTP-001) and the pre-characterization risk assessment (RA-001) | Sending site MSAT |
| Characterization | Master plan (PCMP-001), the plan and report for each unit operation, master report (PCMR-001) | Sending site PD and MSAT |
| Transfer execution | Process description, master batch records, document mapping table, analytical method transfer reports, scale-down model qualification records | Both sites |
| Readiness | Engineering runs, comparability assessment, approved control strategy, gap closure record | Receiving site MSAT |
| Qualification | Qualification protocol, execution of the qualification batches, qualification report | Receiving site |

: Transfer deliverables and the phase that produces them. {#tbl-deliv}

The characterization phase is the long one, and it runs in parallel with the transfer
execution phase for every step whose plan is already approved. The dependency that fixes
the critical path is PCMR-001, because qualification cannot start until the master report
is approved (§7).

# Approvals

This plan takes effect when every signatory in @tbl-appr has approved it. Approval by
Quality Assurance is required at both sites before any deliverable listed in @tbl-deliv is
executed. A change to this plan after approval is handled under change control, and a
change that alters the scope stated in §1 requires re-approval by the same signatories.
